newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle shares to stall, then rise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Nestle shares to stall, then rise - analysts.

text.p: Lower-than expected sales volume growth in the first half could keep Nestle shares under slight pressure for a few days, but the stock seems set to rise later on good long-term growth prospects, analysts said.

"Volume growth was significantly weaker than what I was forecasting and also a little bit weaker than consensus," James Amoroso at Bank Julius Baer said after Nestle said real internal growth excluding acquisitions and divestments rose 2.7 percent, up from 2.2 percent in the first quarter.
"I am a little concerned about volume growth. It is not clear where the problem was," he said.
Shares opened four Swiss francs weaker at 1,965 francs and touched a low at 1,940 before rebounding to be nearly unchanged.

"The share price will probably head down a little more during the course of the day and then it will come back again tomorrow. Nestle is already significantly below the market anyway so I don't think it is going to fall dramatically," Amoroso said before the market opened.
"I would advise caution over the coming days, but I think once the dust has cleared I think people will realise Nestle is still undervalued relative to the market."
Anne Alexandre at CSFB in London said the sales figure of 33.5 billion was just below her forecast of 33.8 billion. She had been looking for 3.1 percent volume growth.
"But I am not too concerned because it still means that the second quarter saw volume growth of three percent compared with 2.2 percent in the first quarter," she said.
"It is still an acceleration despite weather that was not so good in June, despite some difficulties in North American coffee, overall increase in coffee prices. It is not too bad."
She said Nestle would have trouble reaching its target of four percent volume growth this year, and put her estimate at 3.4 percent.
"I think the four percent (target) depended on summer weather. They were expecting a rebound compared with bad summer weather last year."

Any more coffee price rises could weigh on volume by curtailing consumer demand, she said, noting the biggest risk Nestle faced was that frost could hurt Brazil's coffee crop and drive prices higher at a time of low stocks.

"Overall I have a buy recommendation. I still like the stock. I think that if they can achieve close to 3.5 percent for the full year it is still a very good achievement compared with what they have been able to achieve in past years," she said.

"They are positioned in such a way that they have growth in emerging markets even if there are slowdowns in some parts. That I like, and on top of that they are doing the right thing in their traditional markets-- cost cutting."
She suggested buying on the dips.

"We have a stock that is not very expensive and is just about to get into higher growth -- even if it not yet the four percent they have been talking about -- an acceleration compared to what we saw in recent years," she said.
"Cheap valuation and prospects for acceleration together give good prospects for revaluation of the stock. That is why on a 12- or 18-month view I am positive on the company."
